note: Owner-approved targets. A GPU job names one target. Its training tape holds motions listed here and training variants of them (training_variants), and never held_out motions; infra/storage/spend_guard.py notes anything else in the job's spend reflection. Motions not listed are stress tests: they may be evaluated (on CPU) to show limits, but are never trained toward and never drive cost. Changing this file needs the owner's approval and a commit.

targets.approved: 2026-11-07, owner questionnaire: lively tempo, all-fours moves included, hops left out
targets.intent: A 50 cm ape that moves in an agile, playful way, like a little monkey or a baby ape, on parts a hobby budget can carry.
targets.world: Obstacle world (owner, 2026-11-08; control/wbc/parcour.py), home-floor sizes: uneven ground up to 1.2 cm, rolling ground up to 1.5 cm, slopes up to 10 deg, steps 0.5-3 cm on 15 cm treads, box grid up to 1.5 cm, mats and sills up to 2 cm. Furniture and doors: walking around and under, stepping onto low items and pushing light doors open are all in scope, explored by trial and error with no fixed list or hard targets.
targets.training_variants: Mirror images (NAME-mirrored) and arm moves layered on leg moves (LEGS-with-ARMS) of the target motions may be on a training tape, for variety (owner, 2026-11-08: more realism and diversity in the training scenarios to make the controller robust). The held_out motions are never on a training tape: they measure agility on motions the controller has not seen.
targets.score: Agility across all motions (owner, 2026-11-08). The motions below are made-up stand-ins for the kinds of movement an agile ape needs; the final set is not known. Any single motion, and any single family, is irrelevant on its own: never tune a reward, controller, servo or body part for one, and never let one drive a run, a requirement or a cost. Grade over all motions, and over motions the controller has not trained on, as distributions; single-motion values are evidence of where and how motion degrades.
targets.body_note: The all-fours moves were authored for the long-arm body (upper arm x1.6, forearm x1.27, 30 mm 10 g fist, feet x1.3). The body is a design choice that serves this target, not part of it.

how_well.note: Each measure is graded 0-5 with lab.score_guard.grade against the reference scale given (2.5 at the reference, continuous, no threshold). Grades are read per motion and per family, never collapsed into one verdict.

timing.measure: knee lag behind the reference, ms

leg tracking.why: about where motion looks like the reference in clips this week

arm tracking.why: arm play reads clearly at this error in clips this week

planted contact.measure: peak lift of a foot the reference keeps planted, mm
planted contact.why: a visible shuffle starts at a few mm

steps and knuckles.measure: contact agreement with the reference (feet and knuckles)

travel.measure: final position error on travelling moves, cm
travel.why: a 50 cm robot drifting a hand's width

heat.measure: hottest joint RMS current over rated, over the whole target tape
heat.why: leaves margin for long play and warm rooms

push response.measure: peak torso deviation after a 0.2 m/s push, cm

unseen order.measure: leg and arm error on target motions chained in a new order with new blends, rad
unseen order.why: the controller must follow live commands, not one memorised tape
